title: Long-term Live Imaging Device for Improved Experimental Manipulation of Zebrafish Larvae
protocol: Model the PDMS component of the device with desired geometries and attributes in a 3D modeling software.
Create an assembly of a blank mold and the PDMS part.
Generate a negative mold for the PDMS part by creating a cavity corresponding to the PDMS part.
Save the mold design as an .stl file for 3D printing.
Print molds using a photopolymer 3D printer.
Make multiple molds in a single printing if possible.
Clean molds using a fine brush, denatured alcohol, and compressed air.
Gently scrub and remove uncured resin from the molds.
Remove any material from the microchannel regions of the molds.
Post-cure the molds in a UV post cure apparatus for 60 minutes on each side.
Sand the cavity side of the mold with 200 grit sandpaper until all sealing surfaces are in contact.
Lightly sand the surface with 400 and then 600 grit sandpaper progressively to produce smooth flush surfaces.
Measure the depth of the cavity after sanding with a dial indicator to verify it is close to the designed depth.
Clean molds and cover discs by placing them in an ultrasonic cleaner filled with water for 30 minutes or flushing under running water.
Blow dry molds and covers with compressed air.
Clean both molds and covers with isopropyl alcohol and filtered compressed air.
Leave cleaned molds and glass covers in a clean bench or covered petri dish until needed.
Make PDMS by pouring 184 silicone elastomer polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) at a ratio of 5:1 into a plastic cup.
Mix well for 2 minutes with a wooden craft stick, stirring the gel over onto itself.
De-gas mixture in a vacuum desiccator for 25 - 45 min until all bubbles are gone.
Fill each 3D printed mold with approximately 0.75 mL of PDMS using a 10mL syringe until the mold slightly overflows with a meniscus.
De-gas the filled molds for 45 min to remove additional bubbles that may have formed when filling.
Apply a glass cover disc on top of the PDMS-filled mold, pressing the disc down at an angle to prevent bubbles from being trapped.
Use small ratchet clamp to hold the cover disc tightly to the mold.
Cure the PDMS device in the clamped molds at 100°C in an oven for 90 min.
Remove the molds from the oven and allow them to cool until they can be easily handled.
Clamp the mold containing the PDMS device in a bench vice so that the mold's geometries are facing up, parallel to the working station bench.
Release the PDMS pull tab from the mold using flat-tipped tweezers.
Work around the perimeter of the mold with the tweezers (like removing a cake out of a pan).
Use filtered compressed air and tweezers to gently pull the device out of the mold by holding onto the pull tab and blowing air under the device.
Place the PDMS device upside down onto the inside of the cover of a glass bottomed dish so that the restraining tunnel wedges are touching the plastic.
Place the dish cover with upside-down zWEDGI and the corresponding glass bottomed dish into a plasma cleaner with the inner glass facing upward.
Evacuate the plasma cleaning chamber until pressure reaches 500 mTorr.
Set radio frequency (RF) power to high.
Expose the device and dish to RF frequency for approximately 2 min.
Slowly de-pressurize the chamber.
Return the device and dish to a clean room hood.
Remove the PDMS device from the dish cover.
Flip over the PDMS zWEDGI to the correct orientation on the glass by positioning it carefully onto the center well of the glass bottom dish.
Lightly press down on the PDMS device with the back end of the tweezers to ensure no air bubbles are trapped beneath.
Apply pressure around the minute geometries of the micro channels and smooth the PDMS out to the edges.
Place a cover over the device dish before removing from the clean room hood.
Rinse the channels with a minimum of 100 µL 70% ethanol per channel using a micropipette to rinse through the restraining tunnel.
Remove ethanol and rinse 2 or 3 times with double distilled water.
Fill the channels with skim milk (at a concentration of 1% diluted in water) for 10 min at room temperature to minimize adherence of larvae to the glass coverslip of the dish.
Gently submerge the device several times in double distilled water to rinse.
Prepare 1% low melting point (LMP) agarose by combining 100 µL 2% melted LMP agarose with 100 µL 2x Tricaine in E3 buffer pre-warmed to 38 oC.
Maintain the 1% agarose/tricaine solution at 38 oC in a hot block to prevent gelling.
Anesthetize larvae in E3 buffer containing 0.2 mg/mL tricaine until motionless and non-responsive to touch.
Pre-wet the channels with a few microliters of Tricaine/E3.
Pick up a single larva using a wide orifice pipette tip.
Deposit the larvae into the loading channel.
Orient the larva in the loading chamber such that the dorsal side faces the straighter edge and the tail faces toward the restraining tunnel.
Carefully withdraw fluid from the wounding chamber to allow the larva to flow into the restraining tunnel.
Remove most of the liquid while maintaining moisture around the larva.
Place 1% LMP agarose in Tricaine/E3 over the larva's head, filling the loading chamber.
Allow agarose to solidify with the larva in the proper position.
Add Tricaine/E3 to the wounding chamber as needed to maintain hydration.
Repeat this loading process for the remaining 2 channels.
Carefully remove any agarose that seeped through the restraining tunnel into the wounding chamber using a syringe needle.
Add additional tricaine/E3 either just over the agarose or to fill the culture dish, depending on the imaging requirements.
Replace the culture dish lid to prevent evaporation.
Using a sterile scalpel blade, transect the tail fin posterior to the notochord in the wounding chamber.
Add additional Tricaine/E3 if needed and replace the culture dish lid.
Install the zWEDGI device with anesthetized larvae onto an inverted microscope in a stage insert that accommodates a 60 mm glass bottom dish.
Locate the tail of the larva in the upper-most channel, rotating the dish as needed to position the tail correctly.
Image the larval tail as required for the specific experiment.
Remove the zWEDGI dish from the microscope at the end of the experiment.
Euthanize the larvae by placing the zWEDGI on an ice water bath or at 4°C for at least 20 minutes.
Assess the larvae for absence of heartbeat and circulation.
Gently pull on the agar with forceps or pipette to recover larvae individually.
Remove the agar from the head region and use the larva for additional procedures such as fixation, antibody staining, RNA extraction, or protein extraction.
Clean the zWEDGI with ethanol and distilled water after removal of larvae and agar.
Set the cleaned zWEDGI upside down to air dry.
Store the dried zWEDGI covered in a cool, dry location.
Re-coat the zWEDGI with skim milk as needed prior to next use.
